# Project Design Context

Implemented and visually verified on 2026-09-07.

## Project

- Name: futurestaff-dsh
- Product type: Desktop Agent workbench
- Stack: React, TypeScript, Vite
- Color mode: light
- Density: compact

## Sources

- Tokens: Local CSS variables in `plugins/fs-product-hub-ui/src/styles.css`
- Components: Product Hub approval card and workbench shell
- Assets: Local jade preview SVGs; no external asset dependency
- Instructions: Explicit approval is separate from Agent recommendation

## Components

- Installed: ProductHubApprovalCard
- Preferred primitives: Native accessible form controls and semantic regions

## Tokens

- Primary: `#176b4b`
- Background: `#f3f5f3`
- Surface: `#ffffff`
- Border: `#dfe5e1`
- Control radius: `8px`; surface radius: `14px`

## Constraints

### Must

- Keep explicit human approval visually separate from Agent recommendations.
- Render buyer-facing facts from the Product Hub server contract only.
- Include loading, empty, error, expired, read-only, rejected, superseded and published states.

### Avoid

- Decorative gradients or glass effects.
- Excessive nested cards and rounded containers.
- Client-authored tenant, product or publication facts.

## Decisions

- Use frozen product previews on the left and explicit publication controls on the right.
- Collapse to one column below 980px and compact horizontal product rows below 640px.
- Keep the visual package in the FutureStaff product layer; the generic desktop shell remains unchanged.

- None recorded

## Desktop shell refinement — 2026-10-11

The user rejected the current screenshot's visual quality. The shell now uses neutral navigation surfaces,
the existing approved FutureStaff mark, a distinct current-subject row, semantic line icons and a single 46px
system toolbar. Blue is limited to brand and selection. Light/dark tokens are owned by
`plugins/fs-platform-access/src/client/appearance.ts`; earlier green Product Hub approval tokens remain module context.
The former saturated blue sidebar decision is superseded for the desktop frame.
21st catalog search found browser-style sidebar/tab patterns; implementation reuses existing project controls.
